summary:
Rocket Simulator (v0.1.0) is a browser-based 2D rocket-engineering and mission-control game created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It turns aerospace physics equations into hands-on design and flight decisions through an iterative learning loop: build, predict, fly, fail,debrief,and refine.

Gameplay & Features
Players select a commander profile and tackle 5 mission tiers—scaling from a 120 km sounding rocket to a heavy-lift Mars transfer vehicle (150 kg to 100,000 kg payloads; 2.2 to 15.5 km/s delta-v). In the Vehicle Assembly Building (VAB), players fill 10 slots using 42 hardware parts, balancing mass, thrust-to-weight ratio (TWR), delta-v, and aerodynamics (center of mass vs. pressure) with a 30 Hz offline Assembly Check prediction.

During launch, a 60 Hz deterministic physics engine and 10 Hz NASA-style flight HUD guide the rocket through a 7-phase ascent (count, tower, Max Q, staging, ascent, insertion, deploy) with live comms and telemetry downlinks. Players actively control throttle, staging, fairings, deployment, and aborts. Twelve failure modes trigger plain-language debriefs and progressive clues pointing to the exact assembly flaw without spoiling the solution.
NASA Data & Tech Stack
Grounded in NASA open data (1976 Standard Atmosphere, NSSDC Earth facts, and Saturn V, SLS, Orion, RS-25, F-1, J-2, and RL10 specs), the responsive web app uses Next.js16, React 19, TypeScript 5, Tailwind CSS 4,Zustand 5, procedural 2D Canvas art Web Audio SFX,and 93 Vitest tests

===============================================================================

ROCKET SIMULATOR — PROJECT DETAILS

===============================================================================

Project: Rocket Simulator | Folder: nasa-game | Date: 2026-11-15 | Version: 0.1.0 (Vertical Slice)

Context: NASA Space Apps Challenge — Global Judging Submission

Companion Docs: docs/PROJECT_SUMMARY.txt, docs/NASA_DATA_SOURCES.txt

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1. PROJECT OVERVIEW

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Rocket Simulator is a browser-based 2D rocket engineering and mission-control game. Players assemble rockets inside the Vehicle Assembly Building (VAB), test their physics, and fly a 7-phase launch. Instead of random failures, every failure is predictable and explained in simple, plain language.

- 5 Mission Tiers: Progress from suborbital sounding rockets up to a Mars transfer mission.

- 42 Hardware Parts: Distributed across 10 rocket assembly slots.

- Real-Time Simulation: Runs a 60 Hz deterministic physics engine paired with a 10 Hz telemetry display (HUD).

- 12 Failure Modes: Includes an in-app guide, post-flight debriefs, and 3 progressive clues to help players fix issues.

- Local Profiles: Saves progress, mission history, and high scores per commander locally in the browser.

- Quality Verified: Backed by 93 automated tests, clean linting, and a clean production build.

- Design Style: Arcade-sim approach—uses real aerospace principles and NASA-derived numbers tuned for fast, accessible learning.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

2. GOALS AND AUDIENCE

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Target Audience:

- Students, hobbyists, and space enthusiasts.

Learning Goals:

- Understand Thrust-to-Weight Ratio (TWR and pad burns), delta-v and staging dry-mass penalties, Max Q throttle management, aerodynamic stability (Center of Mass vs. Center of Pressure, fins, hammerhead fairings), cryogenic boil-off, ullage settling, and fairing separation timing.

Design Principles:

- Consequences over RNG: Outcomes depend strictly on physics and engineering choices, not luck.

- Guided Clue Discovery: Hints point to the specific slot or subsystem at fault without handing over the exact answer.

- Inspectable Physics: All calculations are deterministic and visible to the player.

- Freedom to Fail: The game warns players about risky designs rather than blocking them from launching.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

3. GAMEPLAY AND CONTENT

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

3.1 Core Gameplay Loop

1. Pick a mission tier.

2. Fill the 10 rocket assembly slots.

3. Review live rocket stats (mass, TWR, delta-v, Center of Mass/Pressure, and warnings).

4. Run the Assembly Check pre-flight simulation.

5. Launch and fly the rocket.

6. Succeed or fail (receiving a debrief and 3 clues if something goes wrong).

7. Refine the design and retry.

3.2 Mission Tiers & Win Conditions

- Tier 1: Ares-I Sounding (Black Brant / Orion)

Payload: 150 kg | Target Delta-V: 2.2 km/s | Win Condition: Reach 120 km altitude

- Tier 2: Falcon-X Medium (Falcon 9 class)

Payload: 17,500 kg | Target Delta-V: 9.4 km/s | Win Gate: 7.65 km/s LEO deploy gate

- Tier 3: Artemis Heavy (SLS Block 1)

Payload: 27,000 kg | Target Delta-V: 11.5 km/s | Win Gate: 8.20 km/s TLI deploy gate

- Tier 4: Saturn-V Legacy (Saturn V / Apollo)

Payload: 45,000 kg | Target Delta-V: 14.5 km/s | Win Gate: 8.20 km/s Lunar deploy gate

- Tier 5: Starship Deep-Space (Mars class)

Payload: 100,000 kg | Target Delta-V: 15.5 km/s | Win Gate: 8.20 km/s Mars deploy gate

How to Win: Reach the target altitude (Tier 1) or hit the velocity gate and deploy the payload after Second Engine Cutoff (SECO) (Tiers 2-5).

Timeout & Early Deploy: Missions time out at 1,200 seconds. Manually deploying the payload below the required velocity gate causes an unstable orbit failure.

3.3 VAB Assembly Slots (10 Slots)

The 10 slots are: s1Engine, s1Tank, boosters, fins, interstage, s2Engine, s2Tank, ullage, fairing, and avionics.

- Part Properties: Each part defines mass, physical dimensions, sea-level/vacuum thrust, specific impulse (Isp), propellant type, nozzle expansion, gimbal range, structural rating, cryogenic insulation, and hammerhead fairing flags.

- Compatibility & Launch Rules: Parts have "soft compatibility"—mismatched parts won't stop you from launching, but they will trigger specific engineering failures. To launch, a rocket must have engines, tanks, a fairing, and avionics (plus an interstage and upper stage for 2+ stage builds).

3.4 Assembly Check

- Runs an offline 30 Hz flight prediction using an autopilot policy.

- Returns CLEAR, INCOMPLETE, or specific risk warnings (PAYLOAD, ORBIT, PAD, CONTROL, STRUCTURE, RESTART, HEAT) alongside speed comparisons and progressive clues.

3.5 Flight Phases & Controls

- 7 Flight Phases: COUNT -> TOWER -> MAX Q -> STAGING -> ASCENT -> INSERT -> DEPLOY -> SUCCESS / Failure.

- Keyboard & UI Controls:

* SPACE: Stage separation

* F: Fairing jettison

* D: Payload deploy

* X: Abort mission

* H: Hold countdown

* Throttle: 0-100% slider plus quick presets (100% and 70%)

* Time Warp: 1x, 2x, and 4x speeds

- Auto-Assist: Optionally handles Max Q throttling, Main Engine Cutoff (MECO) staging, fairing jettison (above 80 km), and payload deployment gates.

3.6 Mission Control

- Telemetry: Displays altitude, velocity, dynamic pressure (Q), G-force, remaining propellant, active stage, velocity shortfall, and active warnings.

- Comms Loop: Event-driven radio callouts across 7 stations: FLIGHT, CAPCOM, PROPULSION, GUIDANCE, RANGE, SPACECRAFT, and MCC.

- Downlink: Tracks Stage 1 beacon, Stage 2 telemetry, payload science data, packet counts, and raw hex frames.

3.7 Failure Modes (12 Total)

Every failure links directly to /failures#<id>, generates a post-flight debrief, and provides 3 clues identifying the problem slot:

1. nozzle_overexpanded — Flow separation caused by using a vacuum nozzle at sea level.

2. cryo_boiloff — Propellant loss and ice buildup from using an uninsulated cryogenic tank.

3. pad_burn — Rocket fails to lift off because Thrust-to-Weight Ratio (TWR) is less than 1.

4. pitch_divergence — Aerodynamic flip because the Center of Pressure (CoP) is ahead of the Center of Mass (CoM).

5. interstage_snap — Structural failure caused by placing a wide hammerhead fairing on a weak interstage.

6. max_q_exceeded — Structural breakup from excessive aerodynamic pressure during ascent.

7. ullage_cavitation — Engine flameout in microgravity due to missing ullage settling motors.

8. early_fairing — Payload damaged by jettisoning the fairing below 80 km in dense atmosphere.

9. crash — Surface impact with the ground.

10. unstable_orbit — Payload deployed below the required orbital insertion velocity.

11. timeout — Mission exceeded 1,200 seconds or ran out of fuel with dry tanks.

12. abort — Manual range safety destruct triggered by the player.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

4. SIMULATION MODEL

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The engine uses standard SI units internally (m, s, kg, N) and converts them to readable aerospace units (km, kN, kPa) in the UI, driving visuals via state snapshots.

- Flight Loop: Fixed 60 Hz physics steps via requestAnimationFrame; the HUD updates at ~10 Hz while the canvas renders every frame.

- Atmosphere & Gravity: Uses the 1976 U.S. Standard Atmosphere (log-linear from 0-100 km, exponential above 100 km). Gravity decreases with altitude via g = g0 * (R / (R + h))^2 where R = 6,371,000 m. Calculates speed of sound from temperature, Mach number, and aerodynamic drag (D = 0.5 * rho * v^2 * Cd * A) using a Mach-dependent drag coefficient (Cd).

- Propulsion & Mass: Thrust interpolates smoothly between sea-level and vacuum values based on ambient atmospheric pressure and throttle setting. Propellant mass flow is calculated as m_dot = F / (Isp * g0), and staging drops Stage 1 dry mass.

- Guidance & Failure Checks: Executes a gravity-turn pitch program (configured by start time, pitch rate, and max pitch) and continuously checks CoM vs. CoP stability. Preflight and in-flight rule engines evaluate failure conditions while suppressing duplicate alerts via a fired-set tracker.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

5. ARCHITECTURE AND CODE MAP

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

App Routes (app/):

- page.tsx (/) — Landing and profile briefing

- game/page.tsx (/game) — Main game shell (GameShell)

- failures/page.tsx (/failures) — Failure reference guide

- about/page.tsx (/about) — Team and project credits

- instructions/page.tsx (/instructions) — Redirect

- globals.css — Global styling

Game Logic (src/game/):

- types.ts — Core TypeScript interfaces

- data/ — parts.ts (42 parts), vehicles.ts (5 tiers), failureGuide.ts, comms.ts, hints.ts, assemblySearch.ts, about.ts

- sim/ — atmosphere.ts, vehicle.ts, engine.ts (60 Hz), failures.ts, preflight.ts (30 Hz), autopilot.ts, validate.ts, launchTimeline.ts

- render/ — LaunchScene.tsx (Canvas 2D renderer), sprites.ts

- store/game.ts — Client-side state management via Zustand + localStorage (zero backend)

- audio/ — sfx.ts, cues.ts

- ui/ — GameShell, VabPanel, PartIcon, TelemetryPanel, FlightHUD, FlightScreen, LaunchFX, LaunchCinematic, PadLaunch, RocketArt, CommsLog, DownlinkPanel, AssemblyCheck, FlightDebrief, FailureList, LaunchDock, ResultModal, SoundToggle, TelemetryChart

Rendering Engine: High-DPI HTML Canvas 2D with Device Pixel Ratio (DPR) capping. Supports both a VAB blueprint view and a live Flight view (engine plumes, falling debris, separating fairings, payload deployment, parallax background, Mach cones, and Earth horizon).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

6. USER EXPERIENCE AND RESPONSIVE DESIGN

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

- Routes: /, /game, /failures, /about, and /instructions.

- Responsive Layout: Built on an h-dvh CSS grid. The VAB adapts from 1 column on mobile to a 2x2 grid on tablets and 3 columns on desktop, anchored by a fixed full-width LaunchDock along the bottom. The VAB canvas reserves 120 px at the top and 72-84 px at the bottom to prevent UI overlap, while the Flight HUD applies safe-area padding for notched phones.

- Accessibility & Performance: Features high-contrast monospace labels, color-coded severity indicators, prefers-reduced-motion support, DPR capping, and zero external image or audio file dependencies (all graphics are procedural and all audio is synthesized via Web Audio).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

7. NASA DATA PROVENANCE

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

All NASA data is public domain, verified as of 2026-11-15, and adapted for gameplay rather than certified flight operations (no NASA logos or seals are used; full audit in docs/NASA_DATA_SOURCES.txt):

1. Atmosphere & Earth: U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976 (NASA TM-X-74335, ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19770009539) and NASA NSSDC Earth Fact Sheet (R = 6,371 km, g0 = 9.80665 m/s^2).

2. Engines:

- RS-25: 1,860 kN sea-level / 2,279 kN vacuum thrust; 366 s / 452 s Isp.

- F-1: 6,770 kN sea-level / 7,770 kN vacuum thrust; 263 s / 304 s Isp.

- J-2: 1,090 kN vacuum thrust; 421 s Isp.

- ICPS / RL10: 110 kN vacuum thrust; 465 s Isp.

3. Boosters & Stages: 5-Segment SRB (15,000 kN sea-level / 16,000 kN vacuum thrust, 620 t propellant) and SLS Core LH2 Tank (1,470 t propellant, 64.6 m x 8.4 m).

4. Vehicles: Artemis Heavy (SLS Block 1 / Orion), Saturn-V Legacy, and Ares-I Sounding (Black Brant / Orion).

5. Setting: Visual styling inspired by Kennedy Space Center's VAB and Mission Control Center (MCC).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

8. NON-NASA DATA AND FIDELITY NOTES

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

- Original & Commercial Elements: Falcon-X (Merlin-inspired) and Starship (Raptor-inspired) commercial tiers, failure rules, trajectories, scoring system, the 120 km sounding target, and all procedural art and audio are original designs.

- Gameplay Tuning (Fidelity Notes):

* Values are scaled for arcade pacing and balance.

* The Artemis stack is displayed at 119.4 m (real SLS is ~98 m).

* SLS core propellant is set to 1,470 t (real is ~1,180 t).

* 5-segment SRB propellant is set to 620 t (real is ~726 t).

* J-2 vacuum thrust is tuned slightly higher than historical specs, and ascent profiles follow custom gameplay curves.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

9. QUALITY AND TESTING

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The codebase includes 93 automated tests across 27 files run via Vitest (npm test), with clean npm run lint and static npm run build checks:

1. Physics calculations, game balance, stock build preflight checks, and autopilot winnability across the campaign.

2. Failure engine rule triggers and duplicate alert suppression.

3. Deterministic flight integration, staging, countdown holds, telemetry downlinks, payload science, and aborts.

4. Preflight assembly risk classification and clue generation.

5. Data completeness across the failure guide, about page team roster, comms logs, and hints.

6. UI server-side rendering, Zustand multi-profile store management, legacy save migration, and VAB layout safe zones.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

10. SAVES AND COMMANDER PROFILES

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

- Browser localStorage Keys:

* orbital-architect-profiles — List of created commander profiles.

* orbital-architect-active — Currently selected commander.

* orbital-architect-save:<name> — Full Zustand game state for that profile.

- Stored Data: Unlocked tiers, high scores, flight history, active mission tier, current VAB build, commander name, and audio preferences.

- Profile Management: Players can create, switch, or reset profiles on the briefing page, and legacy save formats are migrated automatically.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

11. LIMITATIONS AND ROADMAP

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Current Limitations:

- 2D planar physics only (no 3D orbital mechanics, inclination changes, or crosswinds).

- Arcade-simplified vehicle masses, heights, and failure conditions.

- Team bios and portraits currently use placeholders.

- No JSON save export/import or in-app flight history viewer yet.

- Final audio mix QA is still pending.

Future Roadmap:

- Save file JSON export/import and an in-app mission history dashboard.

- Real-time weather integration using NASA open data.

- Synthesized voice callouts for Mission Control.

- Expanded campaign tiers and payload types.

- Replacing team bio and portrait placeholders.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

12. HOW TO RUN AND DEMO SCRIPT

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

- System Requirements: Node.js 24+ and npm 11+.

- Commands:

* Install dependencies: npm ci

* Run development server (port 3000): npm run dev

* Run test suite (93 tests): npm test

* Run linter: npm run lint

* Build & start production app: npm run build then npm start

- 4-Minute Demo Script:

1. Open /, create a commander profile, and click Play.

2. Build a Tier 1 rocket (add engine, tank, fairing, and avionics) while observing live TWR and delta-v updates.

3. Run Assembly Check and inspect the generated clue.

4. Launch the rocket, throttle down to 70% during Max Q, stage when spent, and deploy the payload at target altitude.

5. Intentionally build a faulty rocket (e.g., vacuum nozzle at sea level or an uninsulated cryogenic tank), launch it, and review the resulting failure guide and 3 clues.

6. Browse /failures and /about to view the full failure encyclopedia and project credits.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

13. REFERENCES

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

(All references verified 2026-11-15)

1. U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976 (NASA TM-X-74335)

2. NASA NSSDC Earth Fact Sheet

3-6. Space Launch System (SLS), RS-25 engine, Solid Rocket Booster (SRB), and ICPS/RL10 reference pages

7-9. F-1 engine, Saturn V first stage, and Saturn history PDF

10-12. NASA Sounding Rockets, SLS Reference Guide PDF, and Orion Spacecraft overview

13-15. Kennedy Space Center, NASA Technical Reports Server (NTRS), and NASA Media Guidelines

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

14. TEAM, LICENSING, AND DISCLAIMER

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

- Team: Placeholder entries currently reside in src/game/data/about.ts (/about) and should be replaced prior to final judging submission.

- Licensing: All source code and procedural artwork are original. NASA technical data is in the public domain (no NASA logos or seals are used). SpaceX and commercial names are referenced strictly for educational context.

- Disclaimer: This software is an educational simulation only. Physical values are adapted and rounded for gameplay and do not represent certified flight data. This project is unaffiliated with and unendorsed by NASA or SpaceX.
